title.narrative: Emergency Assistance in response to political crisis in CAR (EA01/2013)

description.narrative:
This project aims to provide emergency assistance to the civilian population of CAR who have been affected not only by the ongoing precarious socio-economic situation but also by political instability. An alliance of various armed groups, known as SELEKA, commenced a rebellion against the ruling Government in December, culminating in a coup d’état in March 2013. This rise to power brought with it intense fighting, causing massive displacement, looting and the destruction of public services and provisions.
CAR Caritas recognises the multifaceted nature of this complex situation and as such, proposes the following actions:
1. Advocacy with national political authorities and international bodies on the restoration of State authority responsibility to protect civilians and uphold peace. 2. Peace building activities, including the training of community leaders on peace dialogue at community level 3. Rehabilitation of looted pharmacies and replenishment of essential drugs 4. Supply of food and coupons to those displaced in parishes and monasteries 5. Distribution of seeds and tools to farmers whose seed banks were looted 6. Provision of tools to CAR Caritas trained artisans whose tool kits were taken during the fighting.
These actions are based on an assessment undertaken by CAR Caritas, CRS, Caritas Africa and RCA in March 2013. Although the project is due to close at the end of November, continued fighting is causing disruption to implementation. It is therefore likely that the implementation period will be extended.
